methods.label: Divide the given powers with a domain qualification
methods.explanation:
The exponent domain matters here. Under the recorded interpretation \(a>0\) with real exponents \(m,n\), the same-base quotient law subtracts the exponents. Since \(a^n=3\ne0\),

\(a^{m-n}=a^m\div a^n=12\div3=4\).

If \(m,n\) are positive integers, raising the two givens to the powers \(n\) and \(m\), respectively, gives
\[
12^n=(a^m)^n=(a^n)^m=3^m.
\]
The left side is even and the right side is odd, a contradiction. Thus the positive-integer interpretation has no solution. Real-exponent laws extend beyond the supplied Grade 8 scope, so the answer is conditional on the recorded real-power interpretation: \(4\).
